That the opposite party as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 236 of 1973 for declaration of plaintiff's title in suit holding Nos. 9/1 and 9/2 and for recovery of khas possession with mesne profits, thereof, in the alternative for a Saham of the plaintiff's share partition of the suit properties, stating, inter-alia, that suit Holding Nos. 9/1 and 9/2 comprise 20 decimals of land which fell in the 'Saham' of Surendra Nath Baska by way of partition. Thereafter, Surendra sold out the same to Jashoda Lal Basak the defendant No. 10 in the year 1941 and delivered possession to her. Thus while in possession she executed a baina nama in favour of the plaintiff on 12-9-56 for the sale of the suit property and on receipt of consideration of Taka 2000.00 delivered him the possession thereof and left for India and never returned nor executed any sale deed. Thus the plaintiff while so possessing the suit land, defendant, Nos. 4-9 raised their claim of title on the suit land, showing their documents (sale deed dated 15-8-37 Exhibit 4). Thereafter, in order to make the suit land free from encumbrances the plaintiff took permanent lease of the suit land from defendant Nos. 4-8 and also purchased the 'rent receiving interest' from them. But the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 dispossessed the plaintiff party from suit Holding No. 9/2 on 10-3-62, as such, the plaintiff was constrained to file the aforesaid suit on 15-8-73 against them. 

 (1) On and from the date of publication of a notification under sub-section (3) of section 17 or under sub-section (1) of section 31, no person shall sublet any land in his khas possession in the area to which such notification relates.
